disease.name: White Grubs
disease.pathogen: Holotrichia spp. (Holotrichia consanguinea, Holotrichia serrata, Holotrichia fissa)
disease.severity_index: Can cause 40–60% yield loss if uncontrolled

environmental_factors.temperature_humidity: Prefers warm, humid environments with loose, sandy soils
environmental_factors.soil_conditions: More severe in moist sandy loam soils with crop residues

region_specific_information.Andhra Pradesh: High infestations reported in red loamy soils of Anantapur and Chittoor.
region_specific_information.Telangana: White grubs are a serious concern in rainfed groundnut areas.

early_stage: Wilting of young plants due to root damage
mid_stage: Grubs feeding on root nodules, causing poor nutrient uptake
Weakened plant stems, making them easy to uproot
advanced_stage: Complete plant collapse due to root destruction
Holes in developing pods, leading to reduced nut formation

crop_rotation: Rotate groundnut with non-host crops like sorghum or maize
Avoid back-to-back groundnut planting in the same field
soil_seed_treatment: Basal application of Phorate 10G @ 5-6 kg/acre before sowing
Seed treatment with Imidacloprid @ 5 g/kg seed for early-stage protection

cultural_practices: Deep plowing before sowing to expose and destroy larvae
Flooding fields for 2-3 days kills early-stage grubs
Encouraging bird predation (crows, mynas) for grub control
biological_control: Metarhizium anisopliae @ 2.5 kg/acre mixed with FYM reduces larval population
Neem Cake @ 100 kg/acre as a natural repellent
chemical_control: Phorate 10G @ 5-6 kg/acre in furrows at sowing
Chlorpyrifos 6 ml/L water for localized infestation
